$comment: v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix. Sixteen stateful packages against ten fault shapes (v2.4 plan 03 added the `aborted` shape and the `hostDeletes` package, decision E8; v2.4 plan 05 added `wiEvidence`, v2.5 plan 01 `wiNormalize`, v2.6 plans 06/04/07 `inner`, `harnessTransport`, `agentBridge` and `chapterSeal`), one row per cell, each either citing the test that demonstrates it or saying what is not yet demonstrated. Generated set, hand-classified status. The guard in src/runtime/faultMatrix.guard.test.ts fails when this file and the code disagree: a missing pair, a row for a pair the matrix does not have, a citation whose test is not in the file it names, or an unproven cell that still cites something. Statuses: covered (a test asserts the designed behaviour for this package under this fault) | partial (a test covers part of it, and the note says which part) | todo (nothing covers it) | na (the shape cannot apply, and the note says why).

extraction|backendUnavailable.note: v2.4 plan 03 D3: a dead backend opens an in-memory breaker keyed by profile (never persisted): reads are held, extraction.enabled is never written, and a probe (5 s/15 s/60 s/300 s, online-status, profile update, Try again) resumes the held queue. A missing or deleted profile is config (not-configured + Repair), not transport. Previously partial: The surface names an enabled-but-unprofiled extraction; no test drives the scheduler itself with no reachable profile. v2.4 acceptance A6 (2026-09-25): a SLOW backend is not a dead one. J7 held reads ~32 min on a queued pod because every probe had a fixed 10 s budget; the probe budget now follows the backoff step (10 s/15 s/60 s/300 s cap), floored by the slowest call the profile answered recently, and any real call that answers on the profile closes its breaker. A refusing host keeps the same probe schedule, and a host that never answers gets one bounded probe at a time.

The backlog's Stop exits cleanly with running:false. Live-found fix (2026-09-24): a read that lapsed on a mutation inside its window (reason window, same epoch) is re-queued as a P0 reread:lapsed over its window re-clamped to the chat, once the rollback that mutation started has settled; it merges into an overlapping queued rollback re-read, and a chat/story switch lapse is never re-read.

scene|beforeHostWrite.note: AE04-S1 closed 2026-09-25. The tracker's host write is refused ({ok:false}, the answer setStoryExtensionPrompt gives when the build has no setExtensionPrompt): sync() records `injected` only on ok, so the next sync writes the same block again and it lands; a permanent refusal is retried on every sync and journaled once with the host's reason; the stored read survives. Control: a write that lands is made once. Before the fix `injected` was set before the write and the WriteResult was discarded by the dep's `=> void` type, so a refusal stuck forever.

scene|afterHostWrite.note: v2.4 acceptance A1 (2026-09-25). The fault after the write is the host losing it: ST's clearChat reassigns `extension_prompts = {}` on every chat load, a same-chat reloadCurrentChat included (script.js:1590, 1712). The tracker used to compare against its own `injected` memo (and the seam against its `lastWritten` memo), so a block ST had dropped was never written again. sync() now compares against the block the host holds (`applied`, wired to readInjectedPromptBlocks in runtime/index.ts) and the seam reads getContext().extensionPrompts. Control: while the host still holds the block, nothing is rewritten. Replaces the na row, which said no post-write fault could be injected.

A judge call cancelled because the chat moved (the epoch signal's case) forces nothing into the next prompt, and is not cached: returning to that chat at the same message asks the judge again and forces its pick. stagecraft|duplicateCompletion.note: AE-01 review (2026-09-25): the old citation ran ONE pass and checked `dueForRun()`, which delivers no duplicate. This test completes one accepted op twice: a second `applyAccepted` for the same boundary starts while the first is held at its host write. Both used to read the op as accepted and write it (2 host writes); applies are now serialized, so it is one host write, one `applied` op in one record and one journal line. Its control ("control: an op accepted while the first apply is at the host is written by the second") proves the second apply is not simply dropped: an op accepted mid-apply is still written, and the first apply's patch no longer erases a record appended during its awaits. The sequential repeat is pinned too ("the same boundary applied again after it finished is a no-op"). The curator pass itself cannot complete twice for one call; a second pass while one is in flight is refused by the hold ("coalesces: one pass per boundary gap, and never while one is in flight"). CR-P22 (2026-10-01): a curator completion re-delivered as a second auto-accepted record at the same boundary writes the entry once; the duplicate op is marked failed, never written twice.

alsoEvidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#the record is written from every input category, cites the original ids and keeps every input in its provenance
chapterSeal|delayedSuccess.note: AS-14 (2026-10-01): every model answer that lands in its own chat is committed in one patch (fold, record, derived, chronicle). The mocked model answers at once; no test holds an answer open across a gate and releases it later.

chapterSeal|delayedError.evidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#a model error leaves no record and frees the seal for the next boundary
chapterSeal|delayedError.note: A non-lapse model error propagates out of the seal job before any write: no record, no fold, and inFlight is cleared so the trigger (which reads the path) seals at the next boundary.

chapterSeal|malformedResponse.evidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#a reply with no record is re-asked once, then a degraded record is written
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#a consequence the judge finds unsupported is re-asked once with the failure listed, then degrades
chapterSeal|malformedResponse.note: A refused parse or a failed verify (code or judge memoryVerify) is re-asked once with the reasons listed; a second failure writes the code-built degraded record.

chapterSeal|duplicateCompletion.evidence: src/runtime/chapterSeal.review.test.ts#control: a re-seal that lands swaps the record in one write, with one chapter_seal row for it
chapterSeal|duplicateCompletion.note: A seal of a chapter part that already has a record returns null, and inFlight refuses a second concurrent seal; the re-seal swap leaves exactly one chapter_seal row. No test delivers one model completion twice.

chapterSeal|backendUnavailable.evidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#with the backend answering nothing the chapter still seals, degraded, and folds its rows
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#never blocks: a judge fallback (no answers) or a use switched off keeps the code-only verify
src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#Q-M7: a final, oversize seal whose every answer fails makes at most six model calls, era merges and saga included
chapterSeal|backendUnavailable.note: Empty answers degrade the record instead of stalling the chapter; a judge that is unavailable or off takes the code-only verify; the call budget bounds the attempts.

chapterSeal|beforeHostWrite.note: The one host write is the chapter title card (/comment), after the save; run.stillOwns() is checked right before it, but no test switches the chat between the save and the announce.

chapterSeal|afterHostWrite.note: The title card is the last step of the seal: nothing is written after the host call, so there is no state for a fault after it to leave half-done.

chapterSeal|persistFailure.note: The seal awaits deps.save (saveMetadata, which swallows its own errors) and does not read the save evidence; a lost save leaves the sealed record in memory, where the next persist carries it. Not tested.

chapterSeal|worldSwitched.evidence: src/runtime/chapterSeal.review.test.ts#a re-seal whose run lapses leaves the old record, its fold and its derived row in place
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#a chat that moves while the judge answers seals nothing
src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#controls: a quiet run, a live-only mention and a chat that moves during the vectors read write nothing
chapterSeal|worldSwitched.note: One RunGuard over the sealed range is checked after every await (scene close, arc pass, each map call, each record call, each judge call, saga, era merges, save); archive recall checks its own run after the vectors read.

chapterSeal|aborted.evidence: src/runtime/chapterRetained.review.test.ts#a model call aborted by a lapsed run seals nothing
chapterSeal|aborted.note: The run signal rides every askText; a lapsed call answers empty and the next check returns null before any write.
